discharge_condition_source.text:
The patient had a cysto and TUR of the prostate. Postoperative course was uncomplicated.
The pathology report is pending at the time of dictation. He is being discharged in satisfactory condition with a good urinary stream, minimal hematuria, and on Bactrim DS one a day for ten days with a standard postprostatic surgery instruction sheet.

diagnosis_explanation: Your prostate gland is larger than normal. This can make it hard for urine to leave your bladder. It might feel like you are having trouble peeing. Your bladder neck is blocked. This is a benign condition. It means it is not cancer.
medication_rationale:
Bactrim DS:
This medicine fights infections. It is a type of antibiotic. It was prescribed to prevent infection after surgery. You may notice an upset stomach or mild rash. These are common and not usually serious. Call your doctor right away if you get a severe rash, have trouble breathing, or feel dizzy.
recovery_trajectory:
**Week 1:**
- You will likely feel tired after surgery.
- Expect some burning when you urinate.
- Drink plenty of fluids to help flush your bladder.
- Avoid lifting anything heavier than 10 pounds.
- Do not do strenuous exercise or heavy chores.
- Call your doctor if you cannot urinate.
- Your goal this week is to rest and take it easy.

**Week 2:**
- Your energy levels may start to increase.
- You might see some light blood in your urine. This is normal.
- Continue to drink lots of water.
- Keep lifting limited to 10 pounds or less.
- Avoid activities that make you strain.
- Call your doctor if you have heavy bleeding or a fever.
- Your goal this week is to walk around your home more.

**Week 3:**
- You may feel more comfortable moving around.
- The burning when you urinate should decrease.
- Keep avoiding heavy lifting and strenuous activity.
- You can start doing light household tasks.
- Your goal this week is to walk for 15 minutes daily.
- Call your doctor if your symptoms get worse instead of better.

**Week 4:**
- You should notice a significant improvement in urinary flow.
- You can likely increase your daily activities.
- Continue to avoid lifting more than 10 pounds.
- Ask your doctor before returning to work or exercise.
- Your goal this week is to walk longer distances.
- Call your doctor if you experience sudden strong pain or continued bleeding.

**When to expect improvement:**
- Many men start to feel much better within 4 to 6 weeks.
- Urinary symptoms will continue to improve over time.
- Listen to your body and do not overdo activities.
- Keep up with your follow-up appointments.
escalation_guide:
CALL 911 IMMEDIATELY
These symptoms are life-threatening. Do not drive yourself.
- No symptoms in this tier for your diagnosis.

GO TO THE ER TODAY
Do not wait until tomorrow. Go within a few hours.
- Inability to pee at all: Your bladder is too full.

CALL YOUR DOCTOR
Call during office hours. Do not go to the ER for these.
- Trouble starting your pee stream: Your prostate may block flow.
- Peeing often in small amounts: You may have an infection.
- Feeling like you cannot empty fully: Urine is backing up.
- Weak pee stream: Your prostate may block flow.
- Waking often at night: Sleep can be hard to get.
